title: Escrowed Network Exception Pathway for Isolated On-Prem Customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers running air-gapped or heavily restricted VPC private deployments have requested scheduled platform upgrades that require transient, tightly-scoped outbound access for package pulls or telemetry handshakes. Current intake lanes force either a full network exception (broad, long-lived egress) or a hard decline, creating security friction and delayed upgrades.

Goal: Design an "escrowed network exception" pathway that enables short-lived, auditable, and minimally permissive network egress windows for verified upgrade events. The pathway should preserve customer security posture (principle of least privilege), provide auditability and rollback controls, and be operable by Redwood onboarding and SRE teams with minimal engineering friction.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests related to scheduled upgrades, image pulls, patch windows, and limited telemetry handshakes for private/VPC/on-prem deployments. Not for continuous data exfiltration or permanent outbound connectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook drafted describing escrowed exception workflow with 5-step approval (Customer Security Contact, Redwood Solutions Eng, SRE Gatekeeper, Scheduling, Audit),
Automated token mechanism defined: time-bound one-time token for egress gateway with expiration and scoping by FQDN/IP and port range
Console UI/CSR flow mock or API contract that allows PM/SRE to request and record an escrow window with metadata (customer, reason, artifacts),
Audit log format finalized and retained for 365 days with links to related change tickets and manifests
Rollback path and no-open-egress policy verified in a tabletop exercise with 2 pilot customers
tasks: Work with Security to define allowed outbound scope template (package registries, CDN hosts, Redwood updater endpoints)
Define API contract and minimal db record for escrow windows (start, end, scope, approvers, artifact links)
Prototype ephemeral token issuance service with TTL and single-use enforcement (SRE lead)
Design Console UI wireframe for 'Request Escrow Window' and internal intake form for Solutions Eng
Author customer-facing guidance and checklist for preflight network posture checks
Run two pilot upgrades with customers CUST-A and CUST-B and capture telemetry and lessons learned
notes: Trade-offs: We intentionally avoid shipping arbitrary long-lived firewall rules. This adds operational overhead for scheduling but reduces security objections from compliance teams.
Edge cases: customers with strictly outbound-blocked bastions will require an operator-assisted proxy bridge; add operator-run workflow in runbook.
Related artifacts: see confluence doc (confluence.redwood.internal/escrow-network-pathway) and security spec (drive.redwood.com/secure/escrow-spec-v1.pdf)
Legal/contract: ENG to coordinate with Sales on templated SOC/AUP language for transient egress windows when sensitive customers require it.
